hypotheses_validated.claim: MAJOR (verifier) fixed: hx_store_wait_any no longer sleeps through a completion that happened before the call. A demand read that completes (or fails) while the caller has not looked at that expert since its miss marks it fresh; wait_any returns at once while anything is fresh, then reports every completion so far (generation counter, O(1)); try_acquire/acquire of an expert clear its flag. With nothing new it still waits for the next completion or out its timeout, so polling a failed expert cannot spin.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced first: the new tests built against the unmodified gen-002 store.c (saved copy) gave wait_any blocking 1000.4 ms with the demanded slab already resident, 1000.2 ms when a hit on another expert came between the miss and wait_any, and in the ARCHITECTURE step 2-4 decode loop (200 ms timeout) 13 lost wakeups with 1 reader and 11 with 4 over 60 tokens (2.6 s and 2.4 s). Fixed store.c, same tests: 0 lost wakeups over 200 tokens x 2 configs on every seed run (e.g. 1546 waits, 278 of them with a missing expert already resident, longest 0.00 ms; 200 tokens in 0.03 s). wait_any_wakeups also asserts: reported once (an uncollected slab, then wait_any(30 ms) >= 30 ms), a slab collected by try_acquire or by a blocking acquire is no news, a demand that failed before the call returns at once (< 500 ms of a 1 s timeout) and then polling waits, a completion during the call ends it (40-1000 ms for a read released after 50 ms). The verifier's suggested epoch (seen = completions after every try_acquire) was rejected because it loses a completion that lands between the miss and a later hit in the same pass; as mutant W6 it fails the intra-pass check and the decode loop (19 and 23 lost wakeups).

hypotheses_validated.claim: MAJOR (verifier) fixed: the four surviving targeted mutants are now killed by deterministic, read-hook-gated tests, both with --quick and in full mode.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Scratch driver (each mutant alone on a copy of store.c, against the final test_store.c; --quick --seed 3 and 5, full --seed 4): M1 LRU hot rule off -> hot_rule now runs LRU too ('LRU: a prefetch evicted an expert used this token'); M2 failed read leaks its slot -> starvation(a): 5 injected failures at the minimum slot count, then all 11 slots demanded at once ('only 6 of 11 slots could be filled'), plus top-k bursts; M4 no work_cv broadcast on release -> starvation(b): every slot acquired, a demand starves, a release alone must start its read within 2 s; M9 acquire breaks holds with reads in flight, and M9b the same in wait_any -> starvation(c): two held slabs, one read gated in flight, another demand starved, a blocked acquire / wait_any must not cause a re-read (4 and 3 reads of 2 slabs under the mutants). M11 (hint on a resident expert no longer protects it) also killed by a new protection variant. All KILLED, none by the watchdog. M3a/M3b (stale starved flag) survive and are equivalent by construction: starved is set only while the demand queue is non-empty and the queue only shrinks in the branch that clears it, so the second clear is redundant; without the first, the flag stays stale only while a read is in flight (loading >= 1), and the only readers that act on it with loading == 0 (break_holds) re-evaluate after the reader's next next_job; the remaining effect is spurious broadcasts.
